coverageNote: Unit = the 4 root-level .md files directly in .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/: ideation-index.md (409 lines), domain-map-proposal.md (451), ideation-cx.md (460), moscow-ledger.md (795). Subdirectories were NOT audited as units; they were opened read-only to follow cross-references before calling anything missing (per the cross-reference rule) and to verify the root index's disk-truth claims. Several instinctive findings were raised and then REFUTED during the devil's-advocate pass and are deliberately not reported: (a) 'D-32 missing from the decision log' — it exists, appended out of order at line 261; (b) 'v1 ~45 Musts arithmetic wrong' — 01(10)+02(9)+05(10)+07(9)+09(7)=45 and v1.5 13(15)+14(10)+15(1)=26 both check out against the ledger; (c) 'D-73 sole-trader rehearsal Operator blocker is untracked' — fully tracked with Owner=User and a deferral target in 16.04 Q-04, 15.07 Q-04 and 16.03.02 Q-02; (d) 'D-75 [OWNER] taxonomy question has no deferral target' — tracked with Owner=User / Deferred To=/create-prd in 01.03.02 Q-03 and 17.08.01 Q-04; (e) 'D-26 says 211/276 pairs while everything else says 206/276' and 'ideation-index.md:62 claims moscow-ledger.md lives one level up when it is in the same directory (and the 1,121 file count double-counts the super-index; disk shows 1,122 .md)' — both are bookkeeping inaccuracies that change nothing an implementer builds; (f) 'domain-map-proposal.md sub-domain lists (e.g. 12 for domain 01) contradict the 6 on disk' — D-35 explicitly makes the disk tree authoritative and the proposal ratified evidence; (g) 'Atomic Payment <-> Rights Transfer cross-cut vanished' — owned by ledger feature 05.06.03 and cx pair #49; (h) 'DAW & Desktop Bridge cross-cut vanished' — governed by D-70(a), which converts it to a prohibition with four named reopening conditions.

The ledger is the artifact /plan-phase consumes, so the stale copy is the one the sequencing stage reads.

findings.failure_scenario: A planner opens moscow-ledger.md (the file ideation-index.md:265 names as the "Full ledger with all 734 features") to run /plan-phase, reads line 4, and re-derives a beachhead across all 195 Musts — producing a v1 that is not 01/02/05/07/09-capture and not ~45 Musts. findings.forcedInvention: For at least 20 non-pending cross-domain pairs — including 6 graded `high` — the per-pair 5-question synthesis (state / trigger / permission / notification / race) does not exist at the location ideation-cx.md says it lives. The IA author must invent the interaction's state ownership, trigger direction, permission gate, notification audience and race resolution from a single summary sentence.
findings.claim: ideation-cx.md asserts twice that per-pair cross-domain synthesis detail lives in the source domain's *-cx.md file, and claims 184/206 pairs carry real synthesis. findings.failure_scenario: The IA author sharding domain 04 needs the 04<->24 contract: who owns the occupational-requirement-vs-discrimination adjudication record, what fires the takedown, which role may disposition a suspended poster's orphaned queue, who is notified, and what happens when a takedown and an application decision race. ideation-cx.md sends them to 04-opportunities-casting/opportunities-casting-cx.md, which never mentions domain 24. findings.failure_scenario: /create-prd reads ideation-cx.md §1 to enumerate platform cross-cuts and gets 25; it reads §1b for anything still to rule on and gets 2 (Timestamped Annotation, Practice-Room Tools). Accessibility therefore gets no platform owner and no promotion ruling, and each of the seven domains the proposal lists for it (01, 06, 07, 13, 16, 19, 20) implements its own accessibility behaviour — the private-copy divergence §1b was written to prevent. Same for the follow/save/watchlist primitive, which the ledger scatters across six per-domain features.

findings.failure_scenario: A band member leaves. Domain 23 must decide whether the departed member retains access to the band's invoices, expenses and P&L for the period they were a member, or loses it immediately. Nothing in the tree assigns that decision to anyone or defers it to a stage, so the BE author implementing band financial visibility picks one (e.g. immediate revocation) while the FE author implementing the departing-member flow assumes historic access survives — and no gate catches the divergence because no open question was ever registered.

findings.claim: The MoSCoW ledger's Rationale column is systematically hard-truncated: 521 of 734 rows are exactly 220 characters and 598 of 734 end without terminal punctuation, most of them mid-word. The recorded reason for a tier placement is therefore unrecoverable for the majority of the 734 features, in the one document that exists to record those reasons.

findings.claim: domain-map-proposal.md attaches a **Personas.** line to all 24 domain sections naming dozens of role labels outside the locked four-persona set, and names "band" as a persona in four of them — directly contradicting D-19, which states Band is an entity and NOT a persona, and contradicting the index's own claim of zero invented personas. Neither document carries a marker reconciling the two vocabularies, and none of the proposal's persona labels carries any of the six required persona fields.

D-35 (ideation-index.md:220) ratifies the proposal but scopes the override to structure only — "Existing 24-folder fractal tree is authoritative; the recovery proposal is ratified evidence, not a competing structure" — saying nothing about its persona vocabulary.
findings.failure_scenario: /create-prd-security builds the RBAC role model from the ratified domain map and provisions roles for "band", "A&R", "union rep", "scene organiser" and "dealer/shop" as first-class actor types, while every one of the 189 domain indexes exposes a four-column Role Matrix (Musician / Producer / Operator / Fan) and models Band as an org entity with membership edges. The two role models cannot both be implemented: a band would be simultaneously a principal and an entity with principals inside it.
